summary: Completed a bounded independent read-only review of the M4 auditor package/verifier and offline SQLite/local-blob recovery implementation. Two supported issues: unaccounted SQLite sidecars bypass restored-state consistency, and special-file input can block the trusted verifier before its regular-file check. Findings bind to pre-correction source pins; this is a software review, not an audit conclusion or certification.

findings.mechanism: SQLite-visible state is not bound solely by the main database file digest while adjacent journal files are allowed. verifyLocalBackup hashes database.sqlite, then opens it through DatabaseSync without refusing database.sqlite-wal/-shm/-journal. restoreLocalBackup requires only the main destination and blob directory to be absent. Existing destination WAL/SHM can therefore overlay the newly copied database; the digest check still passes, artifacts(database) observes sidecar state, and restore can report success with database contents different from the verified backup. Backup-side WAL can similarly alter SQL-visible rows without changing the manifest/main database hash.
findings.evidence: Executed auditor-integrity-repro.mjs: synthetic retained_state initially contained expected; a valid stale WAL contained unexpected-stale-wal. With destination main DB absent and WAL/SHM preexisting, restore returned success, SQL query returned unexpected-stale-wal, mainFileHashMatchesBackup=true, preexistingWalPreserved=true. With WAL/SHM added beside backup/database.sqlite, verifyLocalBackup returned success, SQL still returned unexpected-stale-wal, and mainFileHashMatchesManifest=true. Counterevidence: ordinary fresh-directory restore and main-file/blob corruption rejection pass; COPYFILE_EXCL protects an existing main file. This finding requires existing sidecar files and does not assume an attacker can change an operator-owned parent concurrently.
findings.recommendation: Treat the database and its SQLite sidecar namespace as one unit. Before any verification database open or restore mutation, refuse adjacent -wal, -shm, and -journal in the backup snapshot and refuse all corresponding destination paths, preserving existing sidecar bytes. Retain the documented operator-owned/quiesced parent assumptions. Add regressions using a valid WAL that changes a retained non-artifact row, for both verification and restore.

findings.mechanism: read() rejects symlinks but opens other filesystem types with blocking O_RDONLY before checking stat.isFile(). A FIFO named manifest.json, or a listed FIFO file, blocks open() waiting for a writer; the later regular-file and size checks never run. This defeats bounded verification for malformed extracted-directory input.
findings.evidence: Executed auditor-integrity-fifo-repro.mjs against the trusted source verifier with an isolated directory containing FIFO manifest.json. Child had empty stdout/stderr and had to be killed with SIGKILL after 1500 ms. Source confirms no O_NONBLOCK, pre-open regular-file rejection, or deadline. Counterevidence: generated packages contain regular files, existing tests reject symlinks and oversized ordinary files, and this issue needs special-file input in the extracted directory rather than an ordinary generated ZIP.
findings.recommendation: Reject non-regular final components before open, then open with O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK and retain the post-open regular-file/size checks so a replacement with a FIFO cannot block. Add a short bounded isolated FIFO rejection regression.

limitations: No source files were edited. Only assigned rootrun review/reproduction artifacts were written. Parent owns corrections and regression rechecks; this report intentionally records pre-correction pins and makes no claim about later edits.

No live data, PostgreSQL, Docker, browser, full suite, Git, dependency installs, external providers, or subdelegation were used, per scoped brief. SQLite/local-blob backup assumes all writers stopped and operator-owned parents; hosted database/object-store recovery is outside scope.
No crash/power-loss or hostile operator directory-race testing was performed. The local adapter explicitly does not defend against operator-controlled ancestor replacement races.

Other reviewer owns report semantics and snapshot selection correctness. Inspection of those dependencies was limited to integrity boundaries needed here. scripts/backup-local.ts references docs/operations.md, which was absent in the isolated checkout during this pass; operational documentation delivery is separately owned.

Passing focused tests only establishes the exercised cases. A bundled verifier cannot establish its own trust. Coordinated package rewrites without independently retained pins remain outside the documented authenticity claim; no defect was inferred merely from that stated limit.
